- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates or fails to anticipate sharp drops; increase forecast marginally to account for downside risk.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), leading to overshoot in subsequent days; apply smoothing or lag correction for 3-7 day horizons.
- In high-sentiment periods, model tends to overfit recent trends; use 10-15 day moving average or sentiment-weighted smoothing to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion in volatile markets; adjust downward if sentiment is mixed or declining, especially if recent 7-day average is above 70.5.
- If sentiment history shows a sharp reversal (e.g., 0.9 → 0.1), model often lags in adjusting; apply 2-3 day lag correction to forecast decline.
- In low-sentiment or bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3), model underestimates downside risk; add 1-2% buffer to forecast for 15-30 day horizon.
